name: Vascular-like Classical Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
aliases: Vascular Phenotype of Classical Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Vascular-like Classical Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

criteria.description: Marked skin hyperextensibility with soft, velvety skin texture
Spontaneous arterial rupture or aneurysm formation before age 40
Characteristic facial features including thin lips, narrow nose, and prominent eyes
Family history of vascular complications or classical EDS phenotype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of skin hyperextensibility plus either arterial rupture or two minor criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for COL5A1 or COL5A2 mutations supports diagnosis but is not always conclusive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked skin hyperextensibility with velvety texture
searchTerms: very stretchy, soft, and velvety skin
skin that stretches easily with smooth texture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Spontaneous arterial rupture or aneurysm formation
searchTerms: formation of artery bulges or aneurysms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial features including thin lips and narrow nose
searchTerms: thin lips and narrow nose appearance
distinctive facial features with slim mouth and nose
characteristic facial shape with small lips
scars that are broad and depressed
joints that move beyond normal range

common.symptomName: Thin, translucent skin revealing venous pattern
searchTerms: skin so thin veins are visible

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal fragility with risk of perforation
searchTerms: fragile digestive tract prone to tears
early development of swollen leg veins

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; coagulation studies typically normal
Skin biopsy may show collagen fibril abnormalities
imaging: CT angiography revealing arterial aneurysms or dissections
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL5A1 or COL5A2 genes
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathology demonstrating collagen type V abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: More severe arterial fragility with early rupture
Thin translucent skin without significant hyperextensibility
Predominant skin hyperextensibility and joint hypermobility
Mutations in COL5A1 or COL5A2 without prominent vascular phenotype

redFlags: Spontaneous arterial rupture or aneurysm in young individuals
Severe skin fragility with atrophic scarring
Family history of sudden vascular death
references: Malfait F, Francomano C, Byers P, et al. The 2017 international classification of the Ehlers–Danlos syndromes. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2017;175(1):8-26.

Murray ML, Pepin M, Peterson S, Byers PH. Pregnancy-related deaths and complications in women with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Genet Med. 2014;16(12):874-880.
